identity.description: Apify is a web scraping and automation platform built around Actors (serverless cloud programs), with storage, proxies, scheduling, integrations, and a REST API.
identity.identity_notes: Docs at docs.apify.com describe the Apify platform.

auth.oauth_flows: The hosted MCP server (mcp.apify.com) supports OAuth sign-in via Streamable HTTP. The REST API uses an API token.
auth.token_refresh: Tokens are static. They are shown only once, and you can rotate them.
auth.scopes_notes: API token created on the Integrations page in Apify Console. It can be sent as a Bearer header or as a token query parameter. Prepaid spend-capped tokens run Actors that use limited permissions.

api.rate_limits: Global limit of 250,000 requests per minute. Default per-resource limit of 60 requests per second, with some endpoints at 35, 100, 200 or 350 requests per second.
api.limitations: Some Actors may require limited permissions for prepaid tokens. Clients for Go, PHP, Java, .NET and Rust are experimental.

claims.quote: Add it to your request's Authorization header as Bearer <token> . E.g., Authorization: Bearer xxxxxxx .
Add https://mcp.apify.com to your MCP client. On first connection, your browser opens so you can sign in to Apify and approve access.
You can create an API token on the Integrations page in the Apify Console.
The Apify API is built around HTTP REST, uses predictable resource-oriented URLs, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.
Intuitive methods for working with Actors , datasets , key-value stores , and other Apify resources
The Apify's MCP server ( mcp.apify.com ) allows AI applications and agents to interact with the Apify platform using Model Context Protocol (MCP).

claims.value: 250,000 requests per minute globally; 60 requests per second per resource
claims.quote: The global rate limit is set to 250 000 requests per minute .
The client libraries are a more convenient way to interact with the Apify platform than the HTTP REST API.

open_questions: Free plan limits and credits are not described in the sources.
